For each faulty reading, go across from the vertical scale to the curve and then down to the horizontal scale to find the true current.
Subtract the smaller true current near $0.12\text{ mA}$ from the larger true current near $0.42\text{ mA}$ to get the real increase.
walkthrough: Start from the faulty ammeter readings $0.13\text{ mA}$ and $0.47\text{ mA}$ on the vertical ammeter-reading axis.
Recall the curve converts a vertical ammeter reading into a horizontal true current, so read across to the curve then vertically down.
An ammeter reading of $0.13\text{ mA}$ meets the curve at a true current of about $0.12\text{ mA}$.
An ammeter reading of $0.47\text{ mA}$ meets the curve at a true current of about $0.42\text{ mA}$.
Calculate the real increase as $0.42 - 0.12 = 0.30\text{ mA}$ with units of $\text{mA}$.
